subject: Re: Catergorial versus continuous and missing data

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Catergorial versus continuous and missing data
parts:
On 12/21/23 13:36, Ariadna Albajara Sáenz wrote:
> Question 1: CATEGORICAL
> I have a 4-point 4-item scale, however I have some missing data and I
> was wondering what to do in that case: whether I should just indicate
> "ordered = TRUE":
> cfa (specified_model, data = nameofdataset, std.lv = F, meanstructure =
> T, ordered = TRUE) OR
> I read a paper from Lei et al. 2019 recommending using MLR-CAT in case
> of having missing data:
> https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10705511.2019.1680292
> <https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10705511.2019.1680292>?
> What would you recommend?

If the amount of missing data is small, and you can assume MCAR, then
WLSMV + pairwise deletion is usually ok.

Full casewise ML (FIML), treating the variables as categorical is
probably superior, but not available in lavaan. (Maybe in IRT packages?)

But if the 4-point scales are reasonably symmetric, you may get
reasonable results if you treat the data as continuous, and you use
estimator = "MLR" in combination with missing = "ml" (=fiml)

> Question 2: CONTINOUS
> For continuous variables (5-point 6 item scale), is it necessary to
> indicate missing = "fiml" when using estimator = "MLR" or does MLR uses
> fiml by default?

You need to explicitly set missing = "fiml".

Yves.

messages.author: 580c1540ff71f5be
messages.subject: Re: Catergorial versus continuous and missing data
parts:
Dear Yves,

Thank you very much for your response. Regarding the two R options for the ordinal data.
1. OPTION 1 (estimator = "WLSMV", missing = "pairwise"): There is not much missing data but I cannot assume MCAR (from Little's MCAR Test), then I guess I should not use WLSMV + pairwise deletion, right? Also, the model runs with estimator = "WLSMV" but not when I add missing = "pairwise". It gives the following warning:
Error in stats::cov.wt(X[[g]], wt = WT[[g]], method = "ML") :
  'x' must contain finite values only
(even if I have removed rows with only NAs)

2. OPTION 2 (estimator = "MLR",missing = "ml"): The scale is not really symmetric..., so I guess this option is also not good?

Which one of the two options would you recommend, or would be the "less bad"?

Thank you in advance.
